name: Super Crispy Potatoes (Kenji Method)
desc: Potatoes parboiled in alkaline salted water, roughed up into a starchy paste, and roasted with convection until shatteringly crisp.

source.title: Super Crispy Potatoes (Kenji method)
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 4 lb russet or Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 1/2 to 2 inch chunks
ingredients.prep: peeled and cut into 1 1/2 to 2 inch chunks

ingredients.raw: 2 tbsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 oz Parmesan, finely grated on a Microplane (optional)

steps: Set a rack in the center of the oven and preheat to 425°F with convection on.

Bring the water to a boil in a large pot over high heat. Add the 2 tbsp salt, the baking soda and the potatoes and stir. Return to a boil, then simmer until a knife meets little resistance, about 10 min after it returns to a boil.
Drain the potatoes and let them sit in the pot for 30 seconds so the surface moisture steams off.

Transfer to a large bowl, add the olive oil, a pinch of salt and a few grinds of pepper, and toss, shaking the bowl roughly, until a thick layer of mashed-potato-like paste coats every chunk. Toss in the Parmesan, if using.
Spread the potatoes on a large rimmed baking sheet with space between them. Roast without moving for 20 min.

Loosen any stuck potatoes with a thin metal spatula, turn them, and keep roasting, turning a few times, until deep brown and very crisp all over, 30 to 40 min more. Season with salt and serve right away.
tips: Baking soda breaks down the surface to make a starchy crust.
Boiling first drives off moisture before baking.
Microplaned Parmesan adds flavor and more surface area to crisp.
Convection circulates hot air better. Kenji's Serious Eats recipe roasts at 400°F with convection or 450°F without; this version runs at 425°F convection.
Serious Eats infuses the oil with garlic and rosemary and tosses the fried bits and parsley through at the end if you want to add them.
